persona: cli-solver: engineer (or their coding agent) who owns a slow, stochastic, occasionally crashing/garbage-printing/hanging solver written in another language (Node.js CLI, 8 numeric/bool/categorical flags, 6 instance files, --seed, --time-limit, prints cost on stdout) and wants evolvekit to find a better flag configuration than the defaults and export it for deployment. No API keys: fake provider / param_lhs only.
journey:
All work was done in $S (below: $S; PY = <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe). I never read evolvekit/*.py or tests/. I did not modify the repo. `git status` shows ` M docs/mission/DECISION_LOG.md`, a change I did not make.

**16:55.** I read README.md, docs/new-experiment.md, AGENTS.md, examples/pyvrp (the closest example) and the CLI --help. I built solver/fakesolve.js (95 lines) and gen_instances.js (14 lines). Measured on the defaults, the solver crashes 9% of the time, prints garbage 3.7% and hangs 3%.

**Setup.** I ran `evolvekit init`, then wrote skeleton.py, where the evolve block holds constants plus `solver_flags()`. I also wrote a naive 45-line wrapper evaluator and a param_lhs-only config.

- Attempt 1 failed with `big_step_every: must be >= 1`.
- Attempt 2: preflight failed because the default config itself crashes on seed 1, and the console showed only "exit code 1".
- Attempt 3 (seeds: 1): the run died with a fake-provider traceback. The real cause was my undocumented bool/categorical `# PARAMS` entries, which silently disabled param_lhs.
- Attempt 4 (numeric PARAMS only): the first complete run of my own problem finished at 17:03, about 8 minutes in. Five of its nine children were written off at -1e6 by a single crash, garbage output or hang. One stage timeout left an orphan node.exe, which I killed by PID.

**Defensive version.** I rewrote the evaluator (117 lines): a per-call kill, one retry, per-instance normalisation against baseline.json, failure-count KPIs and per-instance text_feedback. I int-coded the bool and categorical parameters, used seeds: 2 and added a hold-out on solver seeds 1000+.

- Preflight was clean.
- The run did 5 generations of 4 children in 3m13s at $0. The best candidate reached 75.96% of the default cost and left no orphans.
- Redirected to a file, the log stayed empty during the run. `status` worked but says nothing about whether the run is alive.

**Export and validation.** I wrote export_best.py (24 lines) and validate.py (37 lines) because evolvekit has no export command and no fresh-seed validation. On unseen seeds the defaults scored 99.3% and the tuned config 75.3%.

**Resume and probes.**

- I killed the run's own PID mid-generation and resumed. The lock was reclaimed, but the param_lhs random number generator replayed, so 3 of 4 children were duplicates.
- A NaN or missing objective KPI scores -0 and becomes the "best" candidate.
- A non-promoted proxy-only candidate can be reported as the overall best.

Files I had to write for tuning: 300 lines (skeleton 30, evaluate 117, baseline 7, config 85, export 24, validate 37). Total with the fake solver: 409 lines. All background processes I started have exited, and a final process check showed no leftovers.

entries.title: NaN or missing objective KPI silently scores -0 and becomes the run's best candidate
entries.step: My solver sometimes prints garbage. `float('nan')` parses fine in a thin wrapper, so I checked what evolvekit does when the objective KPI is NaN, and when the evaluator does not emit the KPI named in score.objective at all.
entries.command:
PY -m evolvekit preflight --config evolvekit.bad_nan.yaml   (evaluator writes {"kpis": {"cost_pct": NaN, ...}})
PY -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.nan_sometimes.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/nan_sometimes --generations 1   (evaluator emits NaN when ALPHA<0.5, else 80+20*ALPHA; direction: minimize)
PY -m evolvekit preflight --config evolvekit.bad_missing.yaml   (evaluator emits mean_cost, config says score.objective: cost_pct)
entries.observed:
preflight: `stage full  ok  0.1s` / `kpis : cost_pct=nan, unresolved_runs=0` / `verdict : clean (0 failure(s), 0 warning(s))`, exit=0.
run: `gen 0  seed  score=-96` / `gen 1  4 child(ren)  best=-0`; leaderboard `| 1 | g001-c0002 | 1 | -0 | -0 |` ranked above `| 2 | g001-c0003 | 1 | -90.7301 |`; `best score : -0`, `improvement : 96`. The runs.jsonl row for g001-c0002 has score -0.0, kpis.cost_pct nan, rejected False.
Missing-objective case: preflight `kpis : mean_cost=123`, `verdict : clean`; run `seed score : -0`.
entries.expected: A non-finite objective KPI, or an objective/penalty KPI the stage never reported, should fail the stage (failure_score) with a message naming the KPI. Preflight should report a FAILURE such as "score.objective 'cost_pct' was not reported by any stage".
entries.why_it_matters: With direction: minimize, a score of 0 beats every real cost. One garbage solver run that reaches the KPI JSON makes the broken candidate the winner, the archive elite and the parent of later generations, and nothing warns about it. I would have exported a configuration whose only quality is that it made the solver print nan.
entries.suggested_fix: Reject NaN/inf KPIs when the evaluator output is read, with the same style of message used for string KPIs. Make preflight, and the run on the seed, fail when score.objective, score.weights or penalties name a KPI that no command stage reported.

entries.title: Stage timeout kills only the evaluator process; the hung solver child survives as an orphan
entries.step: First run with a thin wrapper evaluator (subprocess.run on node, no per-call timeout). One candidate hit a solver hang, so evolvekit's stage timeout (40 s) had to deal with it.
entries.command:
PY -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/naive3
then: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='node.exe'" | ? { $_.CommandLine -like '*fakesolve.js*' }
entries.observed: runs.jsonl: g001-c0002 last_failure = `stage full: timeout after 40s`. About three minutes after that timeout, and after the run had finished: `13060  6548  node.exe  9/19/2026 5:02:05 PM  node ...\fakesolve.js --instance ...\i5.txt --seed 0 --time-limit 3 --alpha 0.472848 ...`. Checking the parent gave `parent 6548 is gone (orphan confirmed)`. I had to `Stop-Process -Id 13060` myself. With my later evaluator, which kills node itself, no orphans were left.
entries.expected: On timeout evolvekit should kill the whole process tree of the stage command (a Job Object or `taskkill /T` on Windows, a process group on POSIX). Failing that, the docs should say clearly that the evaluator must own the lifetime of its children.
entries.why_it_matters: A real hung solver holds a core, memory and possibly a licence seat forever. At a 3% hang rate over a multi-hour run, dozens of them pile up, and they steal CPU from later wall-clock-bounded evaluations. The README itself warns that this kind of contention silently changes scores.
entries.suggested_fix: Launch stage commands in a new process group or Job Object and kill the group on timeout. Log how many descendants were killed. Add a sentence to README 'Write an evaluator' and to docs/new-experiment.md section 2.

entries.title: Non-promoted (proxy-only) candidates are ranked against full-stage scores; the reported 'best' may never have seen the full set
entries.step: I followed the docs' advice to put a subset at stage 1 and the real thing at stage 2, with the natural objective 'mean cost over the stage's instances'. My two proxy instances are smaller, so their mean cost is lower.
entries.command: PY -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.scale.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/scale --generations 2   (proxy inputs [i1,i2] promote top_k_per_generation: 1; full inputs [i1..i6]; objective mean_cost)
entries.observed: Leaderboard #1 and `best score : -10336.7` is g002-c0007, whose stages_reached is ['static','proxy']. It was never promoted, and archive.json elites[0].id is g002-c0007. The candidate that beat it at proxy, g002-c0008 (proxy -10026.8), was promoted, scored -11129.7 on full, and is ranked #3 below two proxy-only rows. In the real run ($S/runs/real1) the leaderboard also mixes proxy-only rows with full rows. For example `| 5 | g002-c0009 | ... -80.4263 | ... gap - |` is a 2-instance, 1-seed score sitting among 6-instance, 2-seed means. The only hint is that the gap column shows `-`.
entries.expected: Rank and choose elites within the deepest stage reached, or never let a candidate that stopped at an earlier stage outrank one that completed a later stage. At minimum, add a stage column to the leaderboard and a bold warning in the docs that the objective must be on an identical scale at every stage.
entries.why_it_matters: Promotion punishes the better candidate and rewards the one that lost at proxy. The config exported as best was never run on 4 of my 6 instances. It is also likely to become the parent of later generations.
entries.suggested_fix: Compare ranking_score only among candidates with the same deepest stage, preferring deeper ones. Add a `stage` column to both leaderboards. State the scale requirement in docs/new-experiment.md section 3.

entries.title: Bool/categorical entries in `# PARAMS` silently disable param_lhs; the only symptom is an unrelated fake-provider traceback
entries.step: Declaring my 8 solver parameters for the no-LLM operator. The docs only show `"NAME": [lo, hi]` with floats, so I guessed `[false, true]` for the bool and a list of strings for the categoricals.
entries.observed: preflight raised nothing about PARAMS (`stage static ok`). The run printed `gen 0  seed  score=-11159.1` and then a 40-line Python traceback ending in `evolvekit.providers.base.ProviderError: fake provider: no scripted responses; set options.responses or options.responses_path`, exit=1. When I removed the three non-numeric entries and changed nothing else, the same config ran to completion with 0 LLM calls. So the invalid entries had silently made the block ineligible for param_lhs, and the driver fell back to an LLM operator I had not configured.
entries.expected: A config or preflight error such as: `# PARAMS entry GREEDY_INIT: expected [lo, hi] numbers, got [false, true]; param_lhs is disabled for this block`. If param_lhs is the only operator and the seed block is not routable to it, refuse to start and say why.
entries.why_it_matters: Most real solver parameters are booleans and categoricals. The error I got points at the provider, a different subsystem, so a user would go and write a fake_responses.yaml instead of fixing the PARAMS line. I only found the cause by bisecting the PARAMS line.
entries.suggested_fix: Validate the PARAMS line when the skeleton is loaded, and in preflight, and print which keys are usable. Support `{"choices": [...]}` and bool natively, or at least document the int-coded workaround: `[0, 1]` and `[0, 2]` integer bounds do produce integers. Also turn the fake-provider ProviderError into a one-line message instead of a traceback.

entries.title: No way to export the winning configuration; the one documented hint points at a path that does not exist
entries.step: Getting the best flag set out of the run in a form I can paste into deployment.
entries.command: PY -m evolvekit --help ; PY -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir $S/runs/real1 --html $S/board.html ; ls $S/runs/real1
entries.observed: The subcommands are only {init,preflight,run,status,leaderboard}. The leaderboard prints ids and scores but no block, KPIs or parameters. `preflight --help` says candidates are 'saved under a run's candidates/ directory', but the actual location is `<run_dir>/work/candidates/g002-c0008.py`. The README lists the run-dir contents and never mentions work/. I had to write export_best.py (24 lines). It parses runs.jsonl using undocumented fields (ranking_score, stages_reached, rejected), restricts to candidates that reached `full`, imports the candidate file and calls my own solver_flags().
entries.expected: `python -m evolvekit best --run-dir R [--stage full] [--out best.py]` should print the id, score, KPIs, feedback and block, and write the spliced candidate file. For PARAMS-style blocks it should also emit the constants as JSON. The work/ layout should be documented.
entries.why_it_matters: The export is the deliverable of the whole exercise. Every user will end up writing the same script against an undocumented JSONL schema. They can get it subtly wrong, for example by taking leaderboard row #1 when it is a proxy-only candidate.
entries.suggested_fix: Add a `best`/`export` subcommand. Document the runs.jsonl fields and `work/candidates`, and fix the preflight --candidate help text.

entries.title: No fresh-seed validation: `{seed}` is always 0..N-1 and `preflight --candidate` replays the tuning seeds
entries.step: Comparing the tuned configuration fairly against the defaults on solver seeds that were not used during tuning.
entries.observed: It re-ran the winner through proxy, full and hold-out and printed the same numbers as the run (`cost_pct=75.9605 (cv 0.80%)`, hold-out `75.8346`), because the seeds are again 0 and 1. No option on `run` or `preflight` offsets or overrides the seeds. No command evaluates two candidates side by side. To get a real A/B I added `--seed-offset` to my evaluator and wrote validate.py (37 lines): `A: mean cost_pct 99.32 sd 0.85 ... B: mean cost_pct 75.31 sd 0.12 ... paired B-A: mean -24.01`.
entries.expected: Something like `python -m evolvekit validate --run-dir R --candidates best,seed --seeds 10 --seed-offset 5000`, or at least `--seed-offset`/`--seeds` flags on `preflight --candidate`, reporting the paired differences and the spread.
entries.why_it_matters: With a noisy solver, a winner picked on two seeds may just be lucky. Checking that is the first thing anyone has to do before deploying, and the tool provides nothing for it. Hold-out via private_inputs helps, but it also feeds ranking through holdout_penalty, so it is not unseen data either.
entries.suggested_fix: Add a validate/compare subcommand, or seed override flags on preflight. Add a short 'validating the winner' section to the README.

entries.title: param_lhs is parent-independent uniform random search over the whole box, though documented as a 'variant of the block's own constants'
entries.step: Running the only search operator available without API keys, and looking at which parameter values the children received.
entries.command: PY -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/real1 ; then tabulated the constants per candidate from runs.jsonl
entries.observed: The parent g002-c0008 (ALPHA 0.2576, TEMP 59.67, ITERS 8354, TABU 14, score -75.96) produced children such as g005-c0018 (ALPHA 0.116, TEMP 91.8, TABU 46, score -121.4) and g005-c0020 (ALPHA 0.750, TEMP 99.2, score -115.9), which is worse than the solver defaults. Every child is a fresh draw across the full declared range, whoever its parent is. Generations 3 to 5 brought no improvement (`gen 3..5 best=-75.9605`). Sampling is linear only: TEMP was declared [0.1, 100] and was almost never below 3. The README table says 'a Latin-hypercube variant of the block's own constants'. The known-gaps list only says it 'picks one variant per child'.
entries.expected: The docs should say plainly that param_lhs is a global space-filling sample with no exploitation. Better still, offer a local mode that shrinks a box around the parent, and a log-scale flag per parameter.
entries.why_it_matters: For a user with no API keys this operator is the entire optimiser. Parent selection, the archive and the lineage are all decoration here, and later generations cannot refine the incumbent. A user expecting evolution will over-budget generations that statistically cannot beat plain random sampling.
entries.suggested_fix: Document the behaviour. Add `search.param_lhs: {mode: global|local, shrink: 0.5}` and a log-scale marker in PARAMS, for example `{"TEMP": {"range": [0.1, 100], "log": true}}`.

entries.title: One failed solver call writes off the whole candidate; no retry/tolerance knob and no guidance for flaky evaluators
entries.step: Running with a straightforward wrapper evaluator that lets a solver crash, garbage output or hang propagate as a non-zero exit or a hang.
entries.command: PY -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/naive3   (evaluate_naive.py, 3 generations x 3 children)
entries.observed: Five of the nine children scored -1e+06: two `stage proxy: exit code 1`, two `stage full: exit code 1`, one `stage full: timeout after 40s`. The timed-out one (ALPHA 0.47, TEMP 6.8, ITERS 5286, TABU 15) sat inside the solver's good region. With `seeds: 2` the default config itself failed: `ABORT: seed failed evaluation - fix the harness before spending: stage full: exit code 1 (on seed 1 of 2 run)`. The README documents 'The first failing run ends the stage'. At a 10% crash rate per call, over 6 instances and N seeds, almost nothing survives. The run itself was not killed by failures in children, which is good.
entries.expected: A per-stage `retries: N` and/or `max_failed_seeds`, or at least a docs section titled 'your evaluator wraps a flaky external program'. That section should cover a per-call timeout, killing the child, counting failures as a penalty KPI, never letting one bad call exit non-zero, and normalising per instance.
entries.why_it_matters: Most of the evaluation budget goes to candidates that are then discarded for reasons unrelated to their quality. The search is also biased against regions where the solver happens to be flakier. I had to design the retry and penalty scheme myself: 117 lines, of which roughly 60 are pure defence.
entries.suggested_fix: Add stage-level `retries` and `tolerate_failed_seeds`. Add a worked examples/cli-solver/ with a defensive evaluator to copy.

entries.title: Console and preflight say only 'exit code 1'; the evaluator's traceback is hidden in an undocumented runs.jsonl field
entries.step: Diagnosing why preflight failed on my default configuration.
entries.observed: `stage full  FAILED  13.2s x2 seed(s)` / `failure : exit code 1 (on seed 1 of 2 run)` / `FAILURE : stage full: exit code 1 (on seed 1 of 2 run)`. There was no stderr. It also printed `note : stage full ran 2 seed(s); the noisiest KPI varied by 0.00% across them`, although only one seed had completed. The actual cause, `subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['node', ... 'i3.txt', '--seed', '1' ...` returned non-zero, turned up only after a `run`, inside runs.jsonl under `last_failure`. The README never mentions that field, and preflight writes no run dir at all.
entries.expected: Print the last 10 to 20 lines of the evaluator's stderr under `failure :` in preflight and in the run's per-generation output. Suppress the CV note when fewer than 2 seeds completed.
entries.why_it_matters: "exit code 1" is not actionable. With preflight there is nowhere else to look, so I had to re-run the evaluator by hand to see the error.
entries.suggested_fix: Include the stderr tail in stage failure messages and document `last_failure`.

entries.title: `run` exits 0 when it ABORTs because the seed failed evaluation
entries.step: Scripting the run from a wrapper or CI job.
entries.command: PY -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.naive2.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/naive_abort --quiet > /dev/null 2>&1; echo exit=$?
entries.observed: `exit=0`. The run had aborted: runs.jsonl holds 1 row, score -1000000.0, `stage full: exit code 1 (on seed 1 of 2 run)`. The non-quiet output says `ABORT: seed failed evaluation ... fix the harness before spending` and `stop reason : seed failed evaluation`.
entries.expected: A non-zero exit code on abort, distinct from lock refusal (3). The README should document run's exit codes the way it does for preflight.
entries.why_it_matters: An agent or a cron wrapper sees success, goes on to export the 'best' candidate (the failed seed at -1e6), and reports that the tuning is done.
entries.suggested_fix: Return 2 when the stop reason is a harness failure, and list run's exit codes in the README.

entries.title: `run` output is block-buffered when redirected: the log file stays empty for the whole run
entries.step: Running the tuning in the background with stdout redirected to a log file, as one does for a long run.
entries.command: PY -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir $S/runs/real1 >> $S/run_real1.log 2>&1 &   then `cat $S/run_real1.log` at +30 s and +90 s
entries.observed: At +30 s and at +90 s the log held only my own timestamp line, while `status` already showed 5 candidates and generations: 1. All 'gen N' lines arrived at once when the process exited after 3m13s. When I re-ran with `python -u`, the lines streamed as they were produced.
entries.expected: Flush after every progress line (`print(..., flush=True)`, or reconfigure stdout to line-buffered).
entries.why_it_matters: With an hour-long evaluator, the log of a nohup or Task Scheduler run would stay empty for hours, which is indistinguishable from a hang.
entries.suggested_fix: Flush progress output. Mention `status` as the supported way to watch a run.

entries.title: `status` cannot tell me whether the run is alive, what it is evaluating, or how many candidates failed
entries.step: Checking on a running and on a finished or aborted run with the documented tool.
entries.command: PY -m evolvekit status --run-dir $S/runs/real1   (mid-run) ; PY -m evolvekit status --run-dir $S/runs/naive3 ; PY -m evolvekit status --run-dir $S/runs/naive1   (aborted)
entries.observed: Mid-run it prints `candidates : 5 (0 rejected)`, `generations : 1`, `archive : no archive.json snapshot yet`, `best : ...`. It gives no running/stopped state even though `.lock` holds the pid, no current candidate, stage or seed, no elapsed time and no time of the last row. For naive3 it prints `candidates : 10 (0 rejected)`, although 5 of the 10 sit at failure_score after timeouts or crashes, and it shows no failure count or reasons. For the aborted run it prints no stop reason; it looks like a healthy 1-candidate run.
entries.expected: A state line (running pid N / finished: <stop reason> / dead lock), the candidate, stage and seed currently in flight with elapsed time versus the timeout, a count of candidates with last_failure grouped by reason, and wall-clock spent on evaluation.
entries.why_it_matters: With a solver that hangs, I need to know whether the run is stuck or merely slow. runs.jsonl is only appended to at generation boundaries, so `status` is blind for the length of a whole generation.
entries.suggested_fix: Write a small heartbeat/progress file per evaluation and surface it in `status`. Persist the stop reason and add failure counts.

entries.title: Resume replays the param_lhs random stream and discards the in-flight generation; `--generations` semantics on resume are undocumented
entries.step: I killed my own run's PID (taken from .lock) in the middle of generation 2 and re-ran the same command in the same --run-dir.
entries.observed: `reclaimed a stale lock from dead pid 9816` / `resumed 5 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl`, which is good. Then: `g002-c0007 duplicate after 1 attempt(s): duplicate: structurally identical to g001-c0003`, and the same for c0008 = g001-c0004 and c0009 = g001-c0005. Three of the four children in the first resumed generation were re-draws of generation 1 and were rejected, so that generation evaluated one new candidate. The candidate that was in flight at the kill (it was on its 5th of 5 evaluator runs) was lost, because rows are only written when a generation completes. The resumed run then went on to gen 4, so `--generations 3` meant '3 more', not '3 in total'. The kill also left the evaluator and node children running; they exited on their own only because my evaluator has its own timeouts.
entries.expected: Persist the sampler state, or derive it from (seed, number of candidates so far), so that a resume continues the stream. Checkpoint per candidate and stage so that finished evaluations survive. Document whether generations is a total or an increment.
entries.why_it_matters: With an hour-long solver, a killed run loses up to a whole generation of evaluations. It then wastes the next generation's slots on duplicates.
entries.suggested_fix: Seed param_lhs from search.seed plus the candidate counter. Append stage results to a journal as they complete. Document the semantics of --generations.

entries.title: Per-instance and hold-out results are only in undocumented work/stage_out files; the leaderboard has no KPI, stage or failure columns
entries.step: Finding out how the winner did on each of my 6 instances, on each seed, and on the hold-out.
entries.observed: The markdown and HTML tables have the columns `# | id | gen | rank | score | cell | operator | model | lineage | gap | USD`. There are no KPIs, no stage reached, and no reason for a failure (failed rows just show -1e+06). runs.jsonl holds the seed-averaged public KPIs and my text_feedback, which per the README is kept for the first seed only. It holds no hold-out KPIs, only private_score and generalization_gap, and no evaluation duration. The complete per-seed data exists only as `work/stage_out/g002-c0008.full.seed0.json`, `...full.private.seed1.json` and so on, a layout the README never mentions. My per-instance list KPI is stored, but no view displays it. The HTML file embeds the raw rows as JSON, but I could not confirm whether the page displays them.
entries.expected: A per-candidate detail view (`leaderboard --candidate ID`, or expandable rows in the HTML) showing per-stage, per-seed KPIs including list KPIs, the hold-out KPIs, feedback and last_failure. The stage_out layout should be documented.
entries.why_it_matters: An average can hide one instance getting worse. The reason I have a 6-instance test set is to check exactly that.
entries.suggested_fix: Add the detail view. Store private KPIs and per-seed KPIs in runs.jsonl, and document work/.

entries.title: No documented pattern or example for tuning an external non-Python CLI program
entries.step: Working out from the docs how a Node.js solver with CLI flags maps onto 'a Python skeleton with an EVOLVE-BLOCK'.
entries.command: Read README 'Adding a problem', docs/new-experiment.md and examples/pyvrp/ (the closest example, but it tunes a Python library in-process)
entries.observed: Every example evolves Python that the evaluator imports and calls. Nothing describes the pattern I had to invent: the block holds constants plus a `solver_flags()` function, and evaluate.py imports the candidate and shells out. Files I had to write before the first useful result: skeleton.py 30 lines, evaluate.py 117, baseline.json 7, evolvekit.yaml 85, plus export_best.py 24 and validate.py 37, which is 300 lines. The subprocess hygiene, per-instance normalisation and hold-out seed mapping were all my own design. Also, the bare `python` in my stage command ran under `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\PythonSoftwareFoundation.Python.3.13...`, not under the venv running evolvekit. That gotcha is documented only inside examples/pyvrp/README.md.
entries.expected: An examples/cli-solver/ directory, or a docs section titled 'tuning an external program', with a copyable defensive evaluator. The interpreter-resolution note should move into the main README and docs/new-experiment.md.
entries.why_it_matters: This persona is arguably the most common use of the param_lhs path, and right now it starts from a blank page.
entries.suggested_fix: Ship a small external-solver example: a fake flaky solver plus a defensive evaluator. Move the `python` resolution note into the main docs, or have evolvekit substitute sys.executable for a leading `python`.

entries.title: `big_step_every: 0` is rejected, so a no-LLM run cannot switch big steps off
entries.step: Configuring a param_lhs-only run, given that scratchpad_every: 0 means off.
entries.observed: `config error: search.big_step_every: must be >= 1, got 0`, exit=2. The message is clear and carries the key path. I worked around it with big_step_every: 1000. I still had to declare two fake `models` slots, and I did not test whether `models` can be omitted entirely.
entries.expected: 0 or null should mean 'never', consistent with scratchpad_every. There should be a documented recipe for a no-LLM, param_lhs-only configuration.
entries.why_it_matters: It is a small thing. But with no keys, a user worries that a big step or a plateau will trigger a provider call mid-run and crash it, as happened in the PARAMS entry above.
entries.suggested_fix: Accept 0 as disabled. Add a 'no-LLM sweep' snippet to the README.

entries.title: preflight truncates the KPI list and hid my penalty KPI; the CV note is dominated by 0/1 counters
entries.step: Reading the preflight output for my defensive evaluator.
entries.observed: `kpis : cost_pct=99.1026 (cv 1.07%), crashes=1.5 (cv 47.14%), garbage=0.5 (cv 141.42%), hangs=0, runtime_s=..., solver_calls=7.5 ..., ... 1 more`. The one hidden KPI was `unresolved_runs`, the only KPI my penalties use, and it was non-zero on that hold-out. The note `the noisiest KPI varied by 141.42% across them` is about a crash counter going from 0 to 1. It says nothing about the objective, whose cv was 0.71%.
entries.expected: Always show the KPIs referenced by score or penalties, or offer --all-kpis. Compute the noise note on the objective KPI.
entries.why_it_matters: The summary hid the number that changes the score. The noise note pointed me at an irrelevant KPI.
entries.suggested_fix: List score/penalty KPIs first and never elide them. Report the objective's CV in the note.

entries.title: Em-dash in the ABORT message turns into mojibake when output is piped on Windows
entries.step: Reading run output through a pipe in Git Bash.
entries.observed: `ABORT: seed failed evaluation � fix the harness before spending: stage full: exit code 1 (on seed 1 of 2 run)`. The same replacement character appears in the `stop reason :` line.
entries.expected: ASCII punctuation in CLI messages, or stdout forced to UTF-8.
entries.why_it_matters: It is only cosmetic, but it breaks grepping and copying the most important line of a failed run.
entries.suggested_fix: Use ' - ' in messages, or call sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8').

unanswered_questions: Is the run alive right now? Which candidate, stage and seed is it evaluating, and how long has that evaluation been running against its timeout? `status` shows none of this, and the log is buffered.
How many candidates were written off at failure_score, and for what reasons (timeout, exit code or bad JSON)? This cannot be answered without parsing `last_failure` in runs.jsonl by hand.
How did a given candidate do on each instance, on each seed, and on the hold-out? This is only available in the undocumented work/stage_out/*.json files. Hold-out KPIs are not in runs.jsonl at all.
Which stage produced the score shown in a leaderboard row? Is the reported 'best' guaranteed to have completed the last stage? It is not, but nothing says so.
What value types does `# PARAMS` accept: int, bool, categorical, log-scale, conditional? What happens to entries it does not understand?
Does param_lhs sample around the parent or across the whole box? Does search.seed make two runs identical? It appears so: real1 and real2 drew the same candidates.
On resume, is `--generations` / `search.generations` a total or an increment? Are evaluations from the interrupted generation reused?
How do I evaluate on seeds other than 0..N-1, such as fresh validation seeds, without editing my evaluator?
How much evaluator wall-clock time did the run and each candidate consume? No duration is recorded per candidate or stage in runs.jsonl, status or the leaderboard.
Is the `models` section required when only param_lhs is used? Can a plateau or a scheduled big step still trigger a provider call in such a run? I did not test omitting `models`.
Does the stage timeout kill the process tree on Linux or macOS? I could only test Windows, where it does not.
What does `run` return as its exit code for each stop reason? Only preflight's exit codes are documented. An abort on seed failure returned 0.
Does a high kpi_cv on the objective ever flag a candidate as unreliable anywhere, or is it purely informational?
went_well: `evolvekit init` and the examples gave me a working config shape quickly. The first complete run of my own problem finished about 8 minutes after I started reading, and the full defensive setup about 13 minutes in.

preflight is useful. It runs the seed through every stage including the hold-out, prints KPIs with their CV, and shows my per-instance text_feedback lines verbatim. Its exit codes 0 and 2 behaved as documented. It gave clear messages for non-JSON output (`evaluator output was not readable JSON`), for a missing output file, and for a string KPI (`KPI 'cost_pct' was '75.3'; KPIs must be numbers or lists of numbers`).
When the seed fails, the run aborts before spending anything: `ABORT: seed failed evaluation - fix the harness before spending`. That is the right call and it is clearly worded.
A failing child never killed the run. It received failure_score, the run carried on, and the evaluator's traceback was preserved in runs.jsonl under `last_failure`.
The stage timeout was enforced on a hung evaluator and reported as `stage full: timeout after 40s`. Only the grandchild process survived.
param_lhs made zero LLM calls and cost $0. It kept integers for integer-bounded parameters, so the workaround of int-coding a bool as [0, 1] and a categorical as [0, 2] worked cleanly.

`seeds: N` averaging with kpi_cv, and `private_inputs` with my own `holdout` token (solver seeds 1000+), worked as documented. The hold-out penalty correctly docked the default config for an unresolved hold-out run (rank -101.6 against score -100.3).

The search produced a real result. 20 evaluations in 3m13s found flags at 76% of the default cost. My own check on unseen seeds gave 75.3% for the tuned config against 99.3% for the defaults (paired difference -24.0 points).
A stale lock from the killed run was reclaimed automatically (`reclaimed a stale lock from dead pid 9816`). The archive was rebuilt from runs.jsonl without manual cleanup.
The config validation error for big_step_every carried the key path and the offending value.
`preflight --candidate <file>` is a handy way to re-score a saved candidate through every stage, once you know the file is in work/candidates/.
text_feedback is stored per stage in runs.jsonl, so the flag string and per-instance lines from my evaluator could be recovered for every candidate (first seed only).
